overall.sentence: Fermi pockets in clean inner CuO2 planes, metallic behaviour below 1% doping and a d-wave gap on pockets coexisting with AF order were already reported by ARPES in Ba-based five- and six-layer cuprates [21, 22]; what is new is the Bi-based n = 5 to 8 intergrowths (including n = 7 and 8), the wider doping range up to 0.088, and finite IP1 gaps of tens of meV down to p = 0.02.

assessment.claim: 1: Fermi pockets at (pi/2, pi/2) in inner planes of Bi-based n = 5-8 intergrowths, p = 0.007-0.088
assessment.note: Same question and method (ARPES pockets in clean inner planes) as [21, 22]; new in the system (Bi-based intergrowths, n = 7 and 8) and the doping range beyond 0.05.

assessment.claim: 2: abrupt Mott insulator to metal transition upon infinitesimal doping ("new intrinsic framework")
assessment.note: Cited [22] already reported a pocket below 1% doping with sharp quasiparticles as first evidence that the slightest doping makes the Mott insulator metallic; this paper adds a second material family, not the conclusion.

assessment.claim: 3: gapless IP0 pockets and d-wave-like IP1 gap up to about 33 meV, pairing down to p = 0.02
assessment.note: A d-wave gap on an inner-plane pocket was reported in [21]; new are the gap magnitude (vs about 5 meV in [21, 22]) and a finite IP1 gap at p = 0.02, where [22] reported none below 0.04. Uncited 2502.16013 also finds large d-wave gaps in the extremely underdoped inner plane of Bi2223.

assessment.claim: 4: pairing coexisting with strong AF order
assessment.note: Coexistence of a d-wave gap and AF order in the same clean CuO2 sheet is in the abstract of [21], and NMR showed SC/AF coexistence in multilayer cuprates (cond-mat/0601450, review [29]); new only in the Bi-based system and doping range.

assessment.claim: 5: insulating behaviour in single- and bilayer cuprates should be re-evaluated as a disorder effect
assessment.note: [22] makes the same argument (established phase diagram rests on disordered planes adjacent to dopant layers); this paper supports it with a second family.

positioning: The paper sits directly on the Kunisada et al. (2020) and Kurokawa et al. (2023) ARPES work on clean inner planes of Ba-based five- and six-layer cuprates, which it cites and which already reported small pockets, metallicity below 1% doping and a d-wave gap coexisting with AF order. As the searches show, its additions are a new material family reached by spatially resolved laser ARPES on Bi2223 intergrowths (n = 5 to 8, including the first n = 7 and 8 data found), a doping range extended to 0.088, and much larger IP1 gaps that persist down to p = 0.02, in tension with [22]. The closest uncited work is Ideta et al. (2025) on the extremely underdoped inner plane of Bi2223 itself, and a four-layer pocket paper by Jeong et al. appeared after this preprint.

issues.claim: The lightly doped CuO2 plane is intrinsically metallic, with an abrupt transition from the Mott insulator upon an infinitesimal amount of doping.
issues.headline: Metallic state below 1% doping was already reported in [22]
issues.issue: Kurokawa et al. [22] (arXiv:2307.07684) already reported a Fermi pocket below 1% doping with sharp quasiparticles in clean inner planes and called it the first evidence that the slightest doping makes the Mott insulator metallic. The Discussion contrasts this paper's result only with single- and bilayer cuprates and calls the framework new, so a referee will ask what is added beyond a second material family.

evidence.quote: Our findings establish a new intrinsic framework for understanding the doping evolution of electronic structures in disorder-free CuO2 planes.

issues.fix: Credit [21, 22] for the metallic pocket at very low doping where the Discussion states the result, and present this work as confirming it in the Bi-based family and extending the doping range and layer number.

edit.before: Our findings establish a new intrinsic framework for understanding the doping evolution of electronic structures in disorder-free CuO2 planes.
edit.after: Together with the earlier observations in Ba-based five- and six-layer cuprates [21, 22], our findings extend the intrinsic framework for understanding the doping evolution of electronic structures in disorder-free CuO2 planes to the Bi-based family and to a wider doping range.

issues.claim: The innermost-plane (IP0) pockets are gapless while the second-innermost-plane (IP1) pockets show an anisotropic, d-wave-like gap of up to about 33 meV, indicating robust electron pairing down to p = 0.02.
issues.headline: Uncited ARPES study of extremely underdoped Bi2223 inner plane
issues.issue: Ideta et al. (arXiv:2502.16013, 2025) measured by ARPES the extremely underdoped clean inner plane of Bi2223, the host crystal used here, and found a large d-wave gap and a nodal metal rather than pockets; its abstract also states that small pockets form in four- to six-layer cuprates. The paper neither cites it nor discusses it next to its statement that no pockets have been reported in three- and four-layer cuprates.

evidence.quote: Since no reports of Fermi pocket formation have been made in three-layer (n = 3)[23–25] and four-layer (n = 4)[26] cuprates so far, the multilayer cuprates with n ≥ 5 provide an ideal platform

issues.fix: Cite Ideta et al. here and in the gap discussion, compare its inner-plane gap with the IP1 gaps found here, and check the four-layer literature before stating that no pockets were reported for n = 4.
